### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/app.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/app.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/app.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/app.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0943caac806d8462842557cca41a2eeb7df43b96` — the merge of head `98e3434b0e2300491bd6acc474e48b8962a1efb6` into base `e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0943caac806d8462842557cca41a2eeb7df43b96 && git checkout 0943caac806d8462842557cca41a2eeb7df43b96
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b 98e3434b0e2300491bd6acc474e48b8962a1efb6 && git checkout -B drift-repro e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b && git merge --no-ff 98e3434b0e2300491bd6acc474e48b8962a1efb6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e22defb13c171900e2c1c54d1d15c24ed85fe91b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `98e3434b0e2300491bd6acc474e48b8962a1efb6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts, packages/spec/liveness/app.json, packages/spec/liveness/README.md, packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-api-surface.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/app-nav-item-api-data-source.test.ts, .changeset/24332-nav-item-api-data-source.md; objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `0707b4ae37`: packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts, packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx, packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx, packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts, packages/core/src/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.ts, packages/core/src/evaluator/fieldRules.ts. The remainder (`content/docs/references/ui/app.mdx`, `authorable-surface/ui.json`, `liveness/state-counts/app.md`) is generator output read for consistency and is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #24332 body and its four comments (triage `6250784407`, regrade `6255770189`, claim `6257260075`, os-dev-report `6258349182`); PR #24427 body, file list (7 files) and the diff against `main`; the 41 check-runs on the head, all completed, 36 success and 5 skipped, none failed. Governed-surface predicate on the file list: 0 of 7 paths hit the register. Head repo is the base repo, not a fork.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set widening, one optional key on the shared nav base — right.** `BaseNavItemSchema` gains `dataSource: ElementApiDataSourceSchema.optional()`; the head spreads `...BaseNavItemSchema.shape` at nine sites (`object`, `dashboard`, `page`, `url`, `report`, `action`, `component`, `doc`, `group`), and `authorable-surface/ui.json` grows exactly nine `NavItem:dataSource` rows. Every app that parsed before parses unchanged; nothing narrows.
2. **By reference, not restated — right.** The nav door's accept set and refusals are `page.zod.ts`'s own: `read.url` same-origin regex, `method` literal `GET`, the credential-key guidance (`headers`, `token`, …), no `write`, the object binding `{ object }` refused at the `dataSource` path, unknown keys refused. The test compares each refusal with `ElementApiDataSourceSchema.safeParse` on the same value by `code` + `path`, which is the right pin for "one binding". `page.zod.ts` does not import `app.zod.ts` and none of its import set reaches an `app.zod` importer (`api/metadata.zod`, `kernel/manifest.zod`, `kernel/metadata-type-schemas`); the head's Type Check and Test Core runs exercise that graph.
3. **Separator refuses the key with its own prescription — right.** `SeparatorNavItemSchema` is `strictObject(navItemSurface('separator'), …)` and `navItemSurface` folds `SEPARATOR_NAV_ITEM_GUIDANCE` in; adding `dataSource` to that list keeps the separator's prescription complete.
4. **`visible` reads the bound value as `data`, one dialect — right.** `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` turns a bare string into `{ dialect: 'cel', source }`; at the pin, `useNavMemberGates` hands `evaluateNavigationVisibility(expr, evaluator)` to the item guard and that calls the same `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateCondition` a page element's `visibleWhen` uses, so a per-entry `data` root is the same spelling and the same root name as `SchemaRenderer`'s `{ ...ambientScope, data: apiData }`. The premise H3a holds as written.
5. **Declared narrower than any enforcement, marked PLANNED — right.** The describe opens with `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]`, the ledger row is `planned`, and the changeset says no console reads the key. At the pin `passesNavItemGuards` calls `evaluateVisibility(item.visible)` with no per-entry scope, and objectui's `NavigationItemObject` is a plain `z.object` that strips `dataSource`. Prime Directive 10 is met: the claim is as narrow as the enforcement.
6. **`label` and the target keys do not read `data` — right, and correctly not built.** `translateApp` replaces a present label with `apps.APP.navigation.ID.label` whenever the bundle has one (rung 1, by entry id), and `walkNavigation` seeds every present label as a literal; `applyNavTemplate`'s `TEMPLATE_VAR_RE` is single-brace `{name}` with no dots. Both forks are real and the describe says so, so no dialect is declared that the runtime cannot honour.
7. **Group carries its own binding, not published to children — right.** `passesNavItemGuards` evaluates `visible` on every type, `group` included; the describe says each child declares its own.
8. **Liveness row shape — right.** `planned` + `authorWarn: true` + `authorHint` is the README's legal way to make a planned row warn (`liveness-planned-property`); `evidenceScope: cross-repo` names the realm and pins both commits as the README requires; the four children are drilled because an undrilled container must be declared (README, "Undrilled containers must be DECLARED") and `check:liveness` recurses to `MAX_DRILL_DEPTH` 8. The lint flattens one `children` level, so the note's "top-level entries only" is a true description of the warning's reach.
9. **Public type surface — right, no missing artifact.** `NavigationItem` / `NavigationItemInput` gain an optional `dataSource` on each branch; `api-surface/*.json` lists export names and `api-surface-signatures.json` hashes `defineX` signatures by `typeToString`, neither of which an added optional property moves, so no api-surface file belongs in the diff. The generated `app.mdx` carries the nine `dataSource` rows, their `provider` / `read` / `path` sub-tables and the 45 re-rendered `visible` rows, consistent with the generator.
10. **No ADR governs the surface.** `docs/adr` names no navigation data root; ADR-0068 rules the `current_user` object only, which the new `data` root leaves alone. The card's shape choice is the seat's four-axis call in the claim, not a reversal of a recorded decision.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **minor** is right: one optional key on nine published branches, no removal, no rename, no narrowing. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset agree with the diff's direction, and `yes` takes at least `minor`, which it does. The changeset body states what changed, the refusals, what does not read the key, and that it is planned. `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness` are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report `6258349182`):
1. `Part of #24332`, not a closing keyword — right; the label and target halves stay open on the card. `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green.
2. `authorWarn` + `authorHint` beyond the dispatch's `planned` — accepted. The README's rule table makes this the only way a planned row warns, and the warning has a measured consequence (next section, item 3). The `runAction` precedent could not be read in this checkout's 7-commit ledger history; the README is sufficient authority.
3. Four drilled children — required, not optional: an undrilled container fails `check:liveness`.
4. `dataSource` in `SEPARATOR_NAV_ITEM_GUIDANCE` — right (① item 3).
5. `@objectstack/cli` unit tier narrowed locally — the head's `Test Core` shards (6 of 6) are green, which is the verdict.
6. Local battery interrupted and resumed — the check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts; nothing turns on the local run.
7. `origin/main` moved after the branch; not re-merged — right per the after-PR merge rule; the merge-base diff is what was reviewed.
8. Commit trailers model-free, PR footer in the session-URL form — repo rule; accepted.

Open questions (also on the card):
1. **Label fork** — escalated to the seat, not decided here. Option C (a declared path key, `label` stays the translatable fallback) is the one that keeps `translateApp`'s rung-1 meaning and has no silent-override trap, but it is a second data-read spelling beside the CEL root, which the seat's own premise excluded. This record does not widen the spec; the seat rules on the card, with the maintainer where the startup-scope axis bites.
2. **Target fork** — escalated with the same reasoning; option D (two entries, complementary `visible` gates, an app page that finds its own record) is the no-new-key route and should be put to the maintainer beside C.
3. **Narrowing arm (a `data.*` read on an entry without `dataSource`)** — not shipped, correctly: it is BREAKING and needs an ADR-0087 disposition. Reading that answers its option C: `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts` faults on an undeclared top-level identifier, `evalFieldPredicate` turns every not-ok verdict into the fallback, and `evaluateNavigationVisibility` re-runs under `throwOnError`, where differing fallbacks throw and the entry is withheld. So at the pin an entry authored with a `data.*` gate and no `data` in scope is hidden, not shown, provided the shell's ambient scope carries no `data` key (not read here). Escalated to the seat as the carrier card's first item: whether parse-time refusal (A) lands with the renderer half (B) or as its own BREAKING PR.
4. **Refusal and describe wording names a page element on the nav door** — option A (neutral wording in `page.zod.ts`) is right and belongs with #24300, which already owns that file's stale `[PLANNED]` describe; the generated `app.mdx` sub-tables repeat "the element" on the nav door and are regenerated by the same fix. Not a FAIL item: the prescription an author receives is still the correct fix.

Acceptance notes:
- objectui's `NavigationItemObject` strips `dataSource` — verified at the pin; renderer-half work for the carrier card.
- Fault behaviour of an unbound `data.*` read — now read, see open question 3; the `authorHint` ("has no value to read") is true and under-describes the consequence (the entry is withheld at the pin). The carrier card should carry the measured consequence; the hint need not change in this PR.

Out of scope: the `check:platform-checklist` main-red the dev reported (`access-security.json` ABSENT SYMBOL `legacyGrantAnchorRetired`) is not this diff's; `Lint & Repo Gates` on this head is green, so it has either been repointed on `main` since or lives outside that job. The seat files it if it still reds.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24332-nav-item-api-data-source`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WnW7HvfnfHbLg1fpkHX3Mu`

**VERDICT: PASS**
